Goal: Explore the bursty-fan-out workload pattern (agent sessions firing parallel requests in bursts) and recommend whether the contention queue (cheap mode, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D) caps should be tuned — vs adding slots — to improve local utilization and cut remote fallback.

Context (from proxy usage analysis, report window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52):
- Fallback events are highly bursty: 95% of the 1293 fallbacks occur within 60s of a previous fallback (median inter-arrival 4s, p90 21s) — agent sessions fanning out parallel calls.
- 37 requests queued→dispatched local and 17 fell back after the queue caps (fallback_after_queue) in-window; 120 local_dispatch_denied (active=1/2 observed at denial, below the 3-slot capacity).
- The contention queue wakes on `local_active_queries` decrement and lease release; context bypasses are never queued. Adding slots shrinks per-slot context (slots-vs-context trade-off) and raises context-bypass volume, so it is NOT a free win (see report recommendations and LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM).
- Hypothesis to test: with bursty fan-out, queue depth/wait caps (contention_queue_max_wait_seconds, contention_queue_max_depth) may be the binding constraint, and tuning them (or making them mode-aware fast/cheap) may recover more local dispatch than raising slot counts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quantify the burst profile: distribution of concurrent local requests during bursts, queue depth observed, queue-wait durations, and how many fallbacks occurred while the contention queue was non-empty (where derivable from logs).
- Evaluate the expected gain of raising queue caps (wait/depth) vs raising slot counts: projected additional local dispatches saved per window, with the slots-vs-context trade-off factored in.
- Recommend concrete config changes (values for contention_queue_max_wait_seconds / contention_queue_max_depth, per-mode if warranted) with quantified expected impact and risks (latency added by queueing, remote fallback avoided).
- Recommendation recorded as a comment on this work item; create follow-up implementation item(s) if config changes are warranted.
data.title: Explore and recommend contention-queue tuning for bursty agent fan-out: queue caps vs more slots

data.description:
# Intake Brief — LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4

## Problem statement

In the 24h window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52, 29.5% of proxy fallbacks (381/1293) were `local_concurrency_limit`; 76.1% of those (290) fired while llama-server had 0 active local streams, yet the proxy's `local_active_queries` counter read "full" (≥ `session_slot_pool_size`=3). The counter spans the entire proxy request lifecycle (prefill/prompt-eval, contention-queue waits, lease cooldown) — not just token generation — so it may over-count busy and drive unnecessary remote fallbacks while the GPU is idle. The project needs a quantified verdict on why this happens and which levers would most reduce it.

## Users

- **Operator (primary):** Wants to minimize remote fallback spend and idle-GPU waste; needs to know whether `local_active_queries` is over-counting and what to change.
  - *Story:* As an operator, I can see a quantified breakdown of idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` events (prefill vs queue vs lease) so I can prioritize the right fix.
- **Proxy maintainer:** Needs event-level evidence and a concrete follow-up proposal, not speculation.
  - *Story:* As a maintainer, I get a recorded recommendation with linked work items and a follow-up implementation item if warranted, so work can proceed without re-investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Quantified verdict:** Measure actual prefill time from llama-server eval-timing lines (total prefill seconds in window) vs decode/busy time (27.9% busy baseline), and — where derivable from proxy + llama logs — the distribution of time between `local_active_queries` increment and `Stream started` (first-byte). State which contributor dominates idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` counts: (a) prefill before first token, (b) contention-queue waits, or (c) inactive lease/cooldown hold.
2. **Hypothesis verdict with evidence:** Confirm or refute that `local_active_queries` over-counts busy with event-level evidence — e.g., time-aligned trace showing a burst of `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks during a llama-server idle stretch (0 active streams, no queued work) while `local_active_queries` reads full.
3. **Levers evaluated:** Evaluate 2–3 concrete levers to improve local processing time or reduce false-full reads (e.g., count only generating requests toward pool, prefill offloading/batching, adaptive lease timeouts, warm-cache promotion / prompt-cache positioning). Each lever has expected impact quantified from the window data (e.g., estimated fallback reduction, TTFT/prefill delta, or busy-time reclaimed).
4. **Recommendation recorded:** A comment on this work item records the recommendation with evidence, links to related work (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D etc.), and a proposed follow-up implementation work item is created via `wl create` if warranted (discovered-from this item).
5. **Documentation & traceability:** Analysis method, data sources (proxy-usage report + CSVs, llama-server logs for the window), and assumptions/unknowns are recorded in the work item; any follow-up item cites the same sources.
6. **Validation:** Full project test suite passes (no code change expected; if any helper scripts are added they are covered by tests). All related documentation touched is updated; `CHANGELOG.md` is left untouched (release pipeline owns it).

## Constraints

- Investigation-only for this item: no production routing change required; recommendation + follow-up item are the deliverable.
- Data window is fixed: 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52 (1293 fallbacks, 381 `local_concurrency_limit`, 290 idle-time); use the proxy-usage report CSVs and llama-server eval-timing logs for that window as primary sources — do not shift the window without documenting why.
- Do not regress cheap-mode queue invariants (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D, LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I) or lease semantics; any lever that touches them must be flagged as such.
- Must not break `session_slot_pool_size` as single source of truth (LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE).

## Existing state

- `local_concurrency_limit` decision at `proxy/proxy/provider.py:_get_local_concurrency_info` (~1803) compares `proxy.server.local_active_queries` (incremented at proxy request start, decremented at finish) against `session_slot_pool_size` (3, `proxy/config.yaml`). The counter covers prompt-eval/prefill, any contention-queue wait (cheap-mode queue policy, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D), and lease hold/cooldown — not just generation.
- `Stream started` is logged inside `stream_generator()` at `proxy/proxy/router.py:1092` (first-byte), so the report's busy-time metric (27.9%) excludes prefill. Prefill estimate in the item: median prompt eval ~100 tok/s vs avg-max context ~123K → potentially ~20 min for largest prompts.
- Candidate contributors already named: (a) prefill before first token, (b) cheap-mode queue waits, (c) inactive-lease cooldown (`router_helpers.py:_try_acquire_local_dispatch` — "inactive lease (post-request cooldown) reserves its slot").
- Llama-server eval-timing lines and proxy fallback CSVs for the window exist (proxy-usage report at `~/proxy-usage-reports/`).

## Desired change

- Produce the quantified verdict + event-level evidence, evaluate 2–3 levers with quantified expected impact, and record a recommendation comment on this work item linking evidence and related work. If warranted, create a follow-up implementation item (with `discovered-from:LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4`) capturing the chosen lever(s).
- No code change is required to close this item; if helper scripts are added for the analysis, commit them under `proxy/benchmarks/` or `scripts/` with tests.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_get_local_concurrency_info` and `local_concurrency_limit` fallback decision
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (lease acquisition, inactive-lease cooldown), `_increment/_decrement_local_active_queries`, adaptive lease helpers
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `stream_generator()` / `Stream started` logging (busy-time definition)
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — Bounded cross-session contention queue (cheap-mode queue vs fallback)
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `local_active_queries` / `local_active_queries_lock` lifecycle
- `proxy/config.yaml` / `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — `session_slot_pool_size` (single source of truth)
- `proxy/benchmarks/` — Harness for prefill/TTFT measurement if needed to quantify levers
- `docs/llama-router.md` — Routing docs to update if findings warrant
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` + llama-server logs — Data sources for the 2026-08-28/29 window

## Related work

- LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D — Cheap mode: prevent slot-contention fallback (bounded queue); keep context fallback (completed)
- LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I — Core: bounded cross-session contention queue (completed)
- LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM — Evaluate increasing local context size (ctx-size); F2–F5 benchmarks, KV headroom, retention — informs lever 3 (warm-cache) context
- LP-0MTAQNAIH001RN1S — Evaluate hard local-routing cap to stop futile over-slot prefills (fast & cheap) (completed)
- LP-0MTAQNB7J0094X71 — Evaluate KV slot save/restore reuse gap (95% checkpoints unrestored) and /slots 500 storms (in-progress) — slot-state reliability
- LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P — Local Qwen3 dispatch lease held 180s after stream end (completed) — lease-cooldown background
- LP-0MSEHMMBK0062ZPI / LP-0MSE05J53004C6EL / LP-0MSU9RL07004FVGO — Adaptive lease / prefill-lease hazards — lease lever background
- LP-0MSC95VTC008GVR7 etc. (F1–F7 under LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM) — Benchmark harness + KV memory — method precedent

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Llama-server eval-timing lines for the exact window may be rotated/purged → Mitigation: use proxy-usage CSVs + any retained window logs; document coverage gaps; fall back to adjacent windows with note.
- **Risk:** `increment → Stream started` distribution may not be derivable without request-ID correlation → Mitigation: use sampled trace or bound estimate; record unknown rather than guessing.
- **Risk:** Scope creep — "improve local processing time" could expand into unrelated perf work → Mitigation: file extra opportunities as linked follow-up items, not scope for this investigation.
- **Assumption:** `session_slot_pool_size=3` for the window (fast schedule 3/3 per report); verify from `proxy/config.yaml` at window time.
- **Assumption:** Report's "0 active local streams" = no `Stream started` without corresponding stream-end at fallback time; confirm definition from proxy-usage-analysis report.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is an interview needed to scope this investigation?" — Answer: No; description already contains clear goal, quantitative context, candidate contributors, and testable ACs. Decision: proceed to draft without interview. Source: agent evaluation of work-item description (2026-08-31).
- Q: "Should this item include implementation of the chosen lever?" — Answer: No; AC 4 requires a recorded recommendation and a proposed follow-up implementation item if warranted — implementation is out of scope. Source: work-item AC 4 text.
- Q: "Which data window is authoritative?" — Answer: 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52 (proxy usage report window). Source: work-item description Context section.

Execute the pre-registered design in docs/session-compaction-experiment-design.md (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ): replay tasks drawn from logged sessions through three arms (A uncompacted→remote deepseek-v4-flash baseline, B compacted→local Qwen3, C uncompacted→local ceiling where the clamp allows), score blind on the rubric, and report go/no-go against the pre-registered quality bar (B ≥ 0.95×A rubric, completion B ≥ A−3pp, no failure increase) and efficiency gate (≥25% wasted-prefill reduction; TTFT P95 not >20% worse).

- Task suite: ≥30 tasks/arm/mode trigger–cap band + ≥10 extreme (fast >58.3K / cheap >43K triggers; F3/F4 strategies: fast truncate→≤38K, cheap summarize→≤30K)
- Harness: proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py (eval-only, fixture-tested, reuses analyze_context_distribution/correlate + context_pressure machinery; no speculative infra)
- Arm B via Tier 1 machinery (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD) once implemented, else the harness's manual prompt-assembly pass with before/after logging
- Deliverable: metrics CSV + scored report + go/no-go recommendation; gates Tier 1 enforcement (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD)
## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Task suite extracted from logged sessions meets the pre-registered size bands — ≥30 tasks per arm per mode in the trigger–cap band (fast >58.3K, cheap >43K triggers) and ≥10 extreme tasks per mode (>fast cap / >cheap cap), both modes represented.
- AC2: Harness `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` is eval-only (no behavior change, no dispatch), fixture-tested (pytest), and reuses existing F1/F2 machinery (`analyze_context_distribution.py` / `correlate_oversized_sessions.py` patterns, `context_pressure` estimates) — no speculative infrastructure.
- AC3: Three arms executed against the task suite — A uncompacted→remote deepseek-v4-flash baseline, B compacted→local Qwen3, C uncompacted→local ceiling where the clamp allows; arm B runs through Tier 1 machinery (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD) once implemented, else the harness's manual prompt-assembly pass with before/after compaction logging.
- AC4: Quality bar met — mean rubric score B ≥ 0.95 × A (non-inferiority, α = 0.05), task completion B ≥ A − 3pp (paired lower bound), no failure|gate increase in B vs A (α = 0.05); cap gates in B only for non-compactable extremes.
- AC5: Efficiency gate met or explicitly waived as secondary — wasted-prefill tokens reduced ≥ 25% on the risky population (B vs A) and TTFT P95 in B not > 20% worse than A where the same task is servable locally.
- AC6: Deliverable produced and committed — metrics CSV + scored report + go/no-go recommendation with explicit pre-registered verdict semantics (go: quality bar met + efficiency gate met or waived + compaction event logging present; no-go on any quality bar breach).

# Log-based contention queue simulation harness

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO

## Goal

Build a reusable simulation script that replays proxy log dispatch events with configurable queue cap parameters to project additional local dispatches saved under different contention_queue configs.

## Approach

Log-based simulation (replay approach) — parse existing log files, reconstruct dispatch-event timelines, then replay with modified parameters. No config changes or live testing required. (Q2 answer: option A — simulation only.)

## Data sources

- Proxy log files: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (rotated, ~6h files), 90-day retention.
- **Analysis windows:** Pre-2026-08-28 log files (e.g. 2026-08-27, 2026-08-26, 2026-08-25, ...). Aug 28+ windows are EXCLUDED — known anomalous data (Q1 answer: option B — use days before 28-8).
- Key log events to parse:
  - `contention_queue_dispatch` — carries queued_duration, policy, depth
  - `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` — carries queued_duration
  - `status_request` — carries queue snapshot (depth, policy, queued_count, fallback_after_queue_count)
  - `local_dispatch_denied` — active slot count at denial time
  - `Fallback triggered` — fallback reason, timestamp

## Simulation logic

- Parse all cheap-mode dispatch events from the log files, reconstruct per-request arrival/occupancy timeline (2-slot cheap mode, session_slot_pool_size=2).
- Replay the same arrival pattern with configurable `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` and `contention_queue_max_depth`.
- For each simulated config, compute: dispatched, fallback_after_queue, total fallbacks, median/percentile queue wait.
- Default simulation (cap=60s wait, depth=4) must reproduce observed counts within tolerance to validate the model.

## Deliverable

Script under `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_simulation.py` (or equivalent location under `proxy/`), testable, with clear CLI interface — mirroring prior benchmark-tool conventions (compare_results.py / project_session_retention.py style).

## Constraints / knowns

- Cheap mode = 2 slots; queue caps: contention_queue_max_wait_seconds=60 (clamped [1, session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds=1800]), contention_queue_max_depth=4 (clamped [1, 16]).
- The queue only engages when policy=queue AND mode=cheap; fast mode (3 slots, policy=fallback) never queues — simulate cheap windows only.
- 2026-08-29 report-window figures cited in parent (37 queued→dispatched, 17 fallback_after_queue) are from the anomalous Aug-28/29 window and serve only as scale reference, not as the primary dataset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Script parses log files and reconstructs dispatch events for any given time window with ≥95% event coverage across the four event types (dispatch, fallback_after_queue, status_request queue snapshot, local_dispatch_denied).
- Simulation with default caps (60s wait, depth 4) reproduces the observed queued→dispatched and fallback_after_queue counts from the replayed cheap-mode windows within ±10% tolerance.
- Output includes per-simulation summary: dispatched count, fallback_after_queue count, total fallbacks, median/percentile queue-wait duration.
- Configurable via CLI args: `--max-wait-seconds`, `--max-depth`, `--log-files`, `--output`.
- Test suite: unit tests for the core simulation engine (replay known synthetic inputs → verify expected outputs); full project suite passes.

# Burst profile quantification (parent AC1)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1 (log-based simulation harness singleton)

## Goal

Quantify the bursty fan-out profile of cheap-mode traffic from pre-2026-08-28 windows: concurrent local request distribution during bursts, observed queue depth, queue-wait duration distribution, and how many fallbacks occurred while the contention queue was non-empty.

## Deliverables

- A markdown report section (or committed analysis doc under `proxy/benchmarks/` / `docs/dev/`) presenting all quantified AC1 metrics for the replayed cheap-mode windows.
- Any reusable extraction code lives in the T1 harness; this item consumes it.

## Metrics (per parent AC1)

1. **Concurrent local requests during bursts:** distribution of `local_active_queries` (reconstructed from status_request/local_dispatch_denied active counts and stream lifetimes) during cheap-mode burst windows; burst definition from inter-arrival analysis (parent cites 95% of fallbacks within 60s of a prior fallback; median inter-arrival 4s, p90 21s).
2. **Queue depth observed:** distribution of `contention_queue_depth` from status_request snapshots and contention_queue_dispatch lines (which carry depth at dispatch).
3. **Queue-wait durations:** distribution of `queued_duration` from contention_queue_dispatch (dispatched) and contention_queue_fallback_after_queue (fell back, typically = wait cap).
4. **Fallbacks while queue non-empty:** count of `Fallback triggered` (cheap-mode, non-context reasons) that co-occur with queue_depth > 0 (via nearest status_request snapshot within a small time delta), where derivable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All four AC1 sub-criteria (concurrent distribution, queue depth, queue-wait durations, fallbacks-while-queue-non-empty) are quantified from the replayed pre-Aug-28 cheap-mode windows and presented in the report.
- Burst definition is stated explicitly (thresholds used, e.g. inter-arrival window / concurrency floor) and applied consistently.
- Methodology is documented and reproducible (script + command documented, following the conventions of prior benchmark reports).
- A comment is recorded on the parent work item LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO summarizing the burst-profile findings and citing the committed report path (if committed) or the raw script output path.

# Queue caps vs slots projected-gain analysis (parent AC2)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1 (simulation harness), T2 (burst profile)

## Goal

Evaluate the expected gain of raising contention queue caps (wait/depth) vs raising slot counts in cheap mode: projected additional local dispatches saved per window, with the slots-vs-context trade-off factored in.

## Approach

- **Queue-cap scenarios (via T1 simulation):** sweep `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (e.g. 120s, 180s, 300s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` (e.g. 8, 12, 16) over the replayed cheap-mode windows; record projected additional queued→dispatched saved, residual fallback_after_queue, and added queue-wait latency percentiles.
- **Slots scenarios:** model 2→3 (and consider 2→4) slots in cheap mode.
- **Slots-vs-context trade-off (Q3 answer: A — reuse prior findings):** reuse the established trade-off from LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F (more slots → smaller per-slot context → more `large_context_bypass`/`context_too_large` fallbacks). Do NOT run new benchmarks. **If reusing prior findings materially compromises the estimate, flag this prominently in the report** (notify-in-report requirement) and note the caveat in the recommendation.

## Deliverables

- Comparison table: for each scenario (queue-cap variants; slots variants), projected Δ local dispatches saved per cheap-mode window vs current config (2 slots, wait 60s, depth 4), with the context-bypass penalty stated.
- Explicit statement of which lever (queue caps or slots) has higher projected impact and why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Queue-cap tuning projected gain quantified with concrete recommended candidate values (at least 2 wait values and 2 depth values evaluated).
- "Add slots" projected gain quantified with the context-bypass penalty included (per-slot ctx shrink → bypass increase), sourced from prior findings (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F) with citations.
- Headline comparison produced: which lever recovers more local dispatch, with numbers.
- If prior benchmark findings were reused and materially affect the estimate, the report must state this caveat up front.

# Add per-session-classification columns to the hourly summary table

## Problem statement

The proxy-usage-analysis report's "Busy time by hour:" sub-table (inside **Local model utilization**) shows one row per hour of the analysis window with busy seconds and busy-%. Add three columns showing, for each hour, the per-session-classification breakdown of requests started in that hour: % that completed local only, % that started local and fell back to remote, % that started remote-only. Move the table to the top of the report and rename it "Summary by hour".

## Users

- **Operator** — wants a quick glance at per-hour session classification (local-only / fell back / remote-only) alongside busy time, so they can correlate demand patterns with provider usage.
- **Pi agents** — when investigating fallback spikes or remote-only patterns, the hourly breakdown provides immediate evidence without running a separate query.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The existing "Busy time by hour:" table in `_append_busy_section(reporting.py)` is replaced with a table titled "**Summary by hour**" that renders **at the top of the report** (before Session summary), regardless of whether the window has local traffic.
2. The table retains its existing "Hour | Busy | %" columns (busy time semantics and calculation unchanged) and adds three new columns: "Started local, completed local", "Started local, fell back", "Started remote-only". Classification is **per-session**: for each hour, count the sessions whose **first request** started in that hour and classify each by its session journey (local-only / fell_back / remote-only); each cell shows the count plus the % of the sessions started in that hour, matching the Session summary table's "n (pct%)" style.
3. A **Totals** row shows overall busy-time totals plus the overall percentage of sessions across each classification category (matching the existing session summary table's local-only / fell back / remote-only percentages).
4. All existing test suite tests pass after the change; add unit tests for the new per-hour session-classification counting and table rendering.
5. Documentation (SKILL.md) updated to describe the new columns, placement, and rename.

## Constraints

- No changes to the parser or aggregation data model — reuse `SessionStats`'s existing `fell_back`, `local_requests`, `remote_requests` for classification.
- Hourly buckets are keyed by the session's start timestamp (hour of day); same limitation as existing hourly_busy (24h daily reports never collide).
- The table is always rendered (removed the `if b.hourly_busy` guard) — but when there is no session data, the table body shows an empty row or "No data" note.

## Existing state

- `_append_busy_section(reporting.py)` (line ~572) renders `| Hour | Busy | % |` inside `if b.hourly_busy:` block, preceded by the Local model utilization heading.
- `SessionStats` already tracks `start` (first in-window stream time), `local_requests`, `remote_requests`, and `fell_back` (via `remote_move_time`).
- The existing session classification logic (reporting.py lines ~289–291) classifies sessions into `local_only`, `fell_back`, `remote_only` at report level — this pattern can be reused per-hour.
- Related: **LP-0MSVMLM7G009N74N** (completed) — added the totals row and bound hours to window.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — `_append_busy_section` (restructure table), `generate_report` (move call to top), `generate_json_summary` (add per-hour classification data).
- `proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — `SessionStats` (already has needed fields — no changes expected).
- `proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — new tests for per-hour classification counting and rendering.
- `proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — update output description.

## Related work

- **LP-0MSVMLM7G009N74N** — previously added totals row to hourly busy table.
- **LP-0MSG97N2F0090TO9** — added the local busy-time report to the skill.
- **LP-0MSAU6MKS008K0RJ** — original proxy-usage-analysis skill (CSVs + report).

## Risks & assumptions

| Risk / Assumption | Detail | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Hour bucket collision on >24h windows | Existing hourly_busy uses hour-of-day keys; same limitation applies | Document in SKILL.md; 24h daily reports never collide |
| Sessions spanning multiple hours | A session's `start` is its first in-window stream; the session is counted in the start hour only, not its duration hours | Clarified in ACs — classification is by start hour |
| No local traffic → no sessions | Table renders regardless of local traffic; when no sessions, show "No data" or empty table | Explicit in AC 3 |
| Existing busy-time % semantics preserved | The existing Busy/% columns are unchanged in meaning and calculation | Verify in review |
data.title: proxy-usage-analysis: add per-hour request-start classification columns to hourly table

# Feature: Compaction config — summarizer_model + trigger ratio

Add compaction configuration to the proxy server: `summarizer_model` and `compaction_trigger_ratio` (0.70).

## Background

Server-side session compaction (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD) requires a summarizer and configurable trigger ratio. This child adds both, reusing the existing Qwen3 model and the existing `context_pressure` machinery in `proxy/provider.py`.

## Proposed config

```yaml
server:
  compaction:
    trigger_ratio:
      type: float
      default: 0.70
    summarizer_model:
      type: local
      llama_model: Qwen3
    summarizer_ctx_size: 8192
    summarizer_max_tokens: 512
```

The model is **reused** from the existing Qwen3 model — no new model download or loading required. The summarizer call uses a lightweight system prompt and small output budget to minimize latency and GPU contention.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Proxy reads `compaction_trigger_ratio` (default 0.70) and `summarizer_model` (local/Qwen3) from config
- AC2 Config is validated at startup; clear error if summarizer llama_model is not loaded or trigger_ratio is out of range (0.0–1.0)
- AC3 Summarizer call uses a dedicated system prompt for compaction summarization
- AC4 Max output tokens configurable (default: 512); output budget enforced
- AC5 Summarizer ctx-size configurable (default: 8192) to avoid unnecessary KV cache
- AC6 Compaction paths (summary, backstop, remote fallback) use the new config
- AC7 Unit tests: config parsing, validation, defaults, startup error paths
data.title: Add summarizer_model config field for proxy-side session compaction

# Feature: Core summarization compaction (fast + cheap modes)

Implement Strategy C (summarize-first) for both fast and cheap modes.

## Fast mode
- **Trigger:** est_tokens > 58,300 (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285)
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens
- **Retention invariant:** system prompt + very first user prompt always verbatim; recent turns retained; middle folded into summary

## Cheap mode
- **Trigger:** est_tokens > 43,000 (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440)
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens
- **Retention invariant:** same as fast mode
- **Non-compactable:** route remote with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch)

## Retention invariant (both modes)
The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:
1. the system prompt
2. the **very first user prompt** (original task statement/setup)
3. the most recent turns within budget

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a summary injected below the retained first prompt.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 Retention invariant: system prompt + very first user prompt verbatim in all compacted outputs (unit + integration test)
- AC2 Fast trigger fires at est_tokens > 58,300; compacted output ≤ 38K tokens
- AC3 Cheap trigger fires at est_tokens > 43,000; compacted output ≤ 30K tokens
- AC4 Non-compactable cheap sessions route remote with guidance (never silent)
- AC5 Summary injected at top of prompt below retained first prompt
- AC6 Unit tests: fast mode summary path, cheap mode summary path, token budget enforcement, non-compactable routing
- AC7 Composes with slot save/restore — compacted prompts restore cleanly under the persistence cap
- **Depends on:** LP-0MTG6RW3L003X122 (config)
data.title: Core summarization compaction (fast + cheap modes)

# Feature: Truncate backstop (both modes)

When summarization alone cannot bring the session under budget, drop oldest non-first turns as a logged backstop. This is a safety net — never the primary mechanism.

## Behavior
- Only triggers when the summary path still leaves the session over budget
- Drops oldest **whole turns** only — never split a turn
- Never drops: system prompt, first user prompt
- Every backstop event is logged (turns dropped, remaining budget)

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 Backstop triggers only when summary path still over budget after summarization
- AC2 Whole turns dropped — never split a turn; never system/first prompt
- AC3 Every backstop event logged with turns dropped and remaining budget
- AC4 Unit tests: backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, first-prompt protection

- ~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-30/report.md (Generated 2026-08-29 13:14:53, window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52, 1293 fallbacks) + fast_sessions.csv, cheap_sessions.csv, errors.csv (44 slot_save errors), errors.json

## Related work / Invariants
- Must NOT regress contention-queue invariants LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D / LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I (fast mode 99.2% of lcl; queue is not the contributor — keep LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D semantics intact)
